question: to the Commission Irmhild Boßdorf (ESN) Subject:

In June 2026, there was an article entitled ‘From Silence to Strategy: Rethinking Menopause as a European Priority’ in the Media Partner section of ‘The Parliament’ magazine1. In this article, the Members of the European Parliament Maria Walsh (EPP), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Billy Kelleher (Renew) and Christophe Clergeau (S&D), among others, argued that menopause should to a greater extent be seen as a European health, economic and societal challenge. The article was supported by the pharmaceutical company Besins Healthcare (transparency register number: 7859633100766-19). The company describes menopause as a policy area where significant health and economic potential could be unlocked through prevention, awareness raising, improved access to treatment and early intervention. Besins Healthcare is an international pharmaceutical group that specialises in hormonal therapies and claims to be the world leader in this field. 1.

Has the Commission assessed the financial impact of extending or increasing public reimbursement for hormone replacement therapies and other menopause treatments, including the resulting market opportunities for pharmaceutical companies?

How does the Commission ensure that menopause policy initiatives are not influenced by the economic interests of companies which market such treatments and at the same time support campaigns, events or media contributions on the issue?

Has the Commission analysed whether and to what extent industry-supported communication and lobbying activities on the issue of menopause have influenced policy priorities at EU level, in particular in the context of the FEMM report 2025/2074(INI)?
Walsh, Maria, et al. „Time for a European Menopause Strategy?“ The Parliament: Total Politics, Juni 2026, S. 15. Special section Women's Health and Menopause, in partnership with Besins Healthcare. 1
